title: Enhanced cervical cancer classification using convolutional tsetlin machines with transfer learning
new_feature: Hybrid pipeline: frozen ImageNet InceptionV3 feature extractor whose embedding is thresholded to bits and classified by a Convolutional TM, for 4-class Pap smear (liquid-based cytology) classification with clause-based interpretability.

datasets.name_in_paper: Liquid-based cytology (LBC) Pap smear image dataset (Mendeley Data, Hussain et al.)
datasets.input_shape_or_features: RGB images resized to 299x299 for InceptionV3; CTM input = binarised InceptionV3 feature vector (dimension not stated)
datasets.split_as_reported: stratified 10-fold cross-validation with patient-level separation; augmentation of minority classes inside training folds only. Table 2 classification report has support 193 (~20% of 963), split not explained
datasets.booleanization: InceptionV3 feature values thresholded at theta=0.5
datasets.notes: 963 images from 460 patients, 40x magnification (Leica ICC50 HD); classes NILM, LSIL, HSIL, SCC; class-imbalanced (NILM majority).

extraction_notes: Internal inconsistencies: Table 3 average precision/recall are 99.00/98.97 with std ±0.01-0.04, whereas text/abstract give 98.99/98.96 with std ±0.22-0.29 (Table 3 values recorded, text values in notes). 'CTM' operates on a 1-D binarised embedding, so the convolutional aspect is unclear. Table 2 report (support 193) does not match 10-fold CV of 963 images. Table 5 literature comparisons (CNN 94%, CNN 93.3%, ResNet 95-98%, Inception 96-98%) are from other papers on possibly different datasets and were not encoded as results. Near-perfect scores should be treated with caution. Fold-level rows of Table 3 omitted.
caution: Table 3 and the text report different accuracies/std, and the classification report covers 193 samples, inconsistent with the stated 10-fold CV over 963 images.
